title: NCRIC-DSP audit log, June–November 2023 — the six SMPD query entries the Department's 9/17/2026 letter describes
summary:
Seeks the NCRIC Data Sharing Partnership audit log that SMPD's executed Memorandum of Understanding with NCRIC (August 2014, produced under W012376-032026) requires be "maintained for a period of no less than three years to record user access to shared data, including the name and organization of the user accessing via the NCRIC-DSP and the date and time when the data was accessed."

The request anchors on the Department's own September 17, 2026 correspondence, which states that "[a]n audit log file spanning June – November 2023 contains six entries of queries by San Mateo Police Department, including the officer's email address, plate searched, and associated case number." Existence, date range, entry count, and field-level contents are therefore already described by the Department itself.

Record requested: the MOU-required audit log — including, without limitation, the June–November 2023 file described in that correspondence — together with any record reflecting the log's current retention status, location, or disposition, to the extent the log itself is withheld or cannot be located.

The request pre-addresses two anticipated responses:

- **Gov. Code § 7923.600 (investigation records).** The exemption reaches investigatory files compiled by "a state or local police agency." The log records access via the NCRIC-DSP generally, not solely by SMPD personnel, and by the Department's own description already involves a non-SMPD organization. Entries reflecting access by federal law enforcement, by a private entity, or by an employee or contractor of NCRIC's vendor are not on their face an investigation by a state or local police agency. Asks that any entries withheld on this basis be identified by the organization associated with the accessing user, without disclosing the user's identity if separately exempt.
- **"PRA NCRIC directly" as a response basis.** MOU § 6 (Information Ownership and Release) provides that "Member Agencies remain the official custodian of all information contributed to the NCRIC-DSP" and that PRA/FOIA requests for a Member Agency's data "will be referred to the Member Agency that is the owner of the requested data," which "will be responsible for responding to the request." The request is submitted to SMPD as that Member Agency, and asks that any deflection to NCRIC identify the MOU provision, statute, or other authority relied on.

Also asks for segregability under § 7922.525(b), exemption citations under § 7922.540, the withheld volume and date range, and — if the log no longer exists or cannot be located — when and why, plus any record reflecting its disposition.

policy_promises.policy: SMPD–NCRIC Memorandum of Understanding (August 2014), general provisions
policy_promises.quote: An audit log will be maintained for a period of no less than three years to record user access to shared data, including the name and organization of the user accessing via the NCRIC-DSP and the date and time when the data was accessed.
policy_promises.tests: Whether the June–November 2023 log still exists. The three-year retention floor was still running when the log surfaced publicly; a "no longer retained" answer has to reconcile with it.

policy_promises.policy: SMPD–NCRIC Memorandum of Understanding, § 6 (Information Ownership and Release)
policy_promises.quote: Member Agencies remain the official custodian of all information contributed to the NCRIC-DSP. To the fullest extent permissible by law, all requests for information, California Public Records Act, or Freedom of Information Act, will be referred to the Member Agency that is the owner of the requested data, and the Member Agency that is the owner of the requested data will be responsible for responding to the request.
policy_promises.tests: Whether SMPD may route this request to NCRIC. § 6 is a referral clause running the other direction — it makes SMPD the responding agency for its own contributed data.

policy_promises.quote: An audit log file spanning June – November 2023 contains six entries of queries by San Mateo Police Department, including the officer's email address, plate searched, and associated case number.
policy_promises.tests: The Department has already described the record down to its fields. A "no responsive records" answer would contradict its own letter.

policy_promises.quote: records of investigations conducted by ... a state or local police agency
policy_promises.tests: Whether entries reflecting access by federal, private-entity, or vendor personnel can be withheld as a state or local police agency's investigatory file.

prior_pra_refs.note: Produced the August 2014 SMPD–NCRIC Memorandum of Understanding, including the audit-log retention provision and § 6, both quoted in this request.

filed_because: The Department's September 17, 2026 correspondence put the record's existence beyond dispute — it names the date span, the entry count, and the fields each entry carries. What it does not do is produce the log, and the MOU's three-year retention floor means a June–November 2023 log should still have been retained. This request converts the Department's own description into a records demand, and forecloses in advance the two responses most likely to be used against it: a blanket § 7923.600 claim over a multi-organization access log, and a referral to NCRIC that MOU § 6 points back at SMPD.
notes:
Filed 2026-09-18. Closed 2026-09-22 (4 days) by Kelly O'Keefe, Police Technical Services Administrator: "A good faith and diligent search yielded no records responsive to your request." No exemption was cited, no volume or date range identified, and the alternative question — whether the log still exists, and if not when and why it was destroyed — went unanswered.

The response directly contradicts the Department's own September 17, 2026 correspondence, which describes the record down to its fields: "[a]n audit log file spanning June - November 2023 contains six entries of queries by San Mateo Police Department, including the officer's email address, plate searched, and associated case number." A no-responsive-records answer five days later is either a search that did not reach the record the Department had just quoted, or an assertion that the record is not SMPD's — a position MOU § 6 forecloses, and which the response does not state or defend.

The MOU's three-year retention floor was still running for a June-November 2023 log at the time of the request, so "no records" also implicates the retention obligation itself. Item 4 of the request specifically asked, if the log no longer exists, when and why; the closure did not respond to it.
